section: Educational Psychology · Ch2 — Piaget: Cognitive Development
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: Piaget's term for the overall process by which a child adjusts their cognitive structures to fit environmental demands, encompassing both assimilation and accommodation, is:
explanation: Adaptation is Piaget's umbrella term for the twin processes of assimilation and accommodation working together to help the organism fit its environment.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch2 — Piaget: Cognitive Development
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A toddler who watches her older brother throw a tantrum at a shop, and then repeats the same behaviour at home hours later, is demonstrating:
explanation: Deferred imitation — copying a behaviour observed earlier, after a time delay — emerges toward the end of the sensorimotor stage and requires mental representation of the observed act.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch2 — Piaget: Cognitive Development
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: The ability to arrange objects in a logical sequence based on a single property, such as lining up sticks from shortest to longest, is called:
explanation: Seriation is a concrete-operational ability (7-11 years) — ordering objects along a quantifiable dimension. It is absent in pre-operational children, who struggle to systematically compare more than two items at once.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch2 — Piaget: Cognitive Development
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: When shown a set of 6 red beads and 2 blue beads (all wooden), a pre-operational child asked 'are there more red beads or more wooden beads?' typically answers 'more red beads' — incorrectly comparing a subclass to the whole class. This reveals a difficulty with:
explanation: Class inclusion — understanding that a subclass (red beads) is necessarily smaller than or equal to the whole class (wooden beads) it belongs to — is a concrete-operational achievement Piaget's beads task famously tests.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch2 — Piaget: Cognitive Development
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A three-year-old uses a banana as a pretend telephone during play. This use of one object to represent another reflects the emergence of:

options.option_text: The symbolic function, characteristic of the pre-operational stage

explanation: The symbolic function — using one thing to stand for another (a banana as a phone) — marks the transition into the pre-operational stage, enabling pretend play and early language.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch2 — Piaget: Cognitive Development
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A pre-operational child reasons: 'I had a nap, and then it got dark, so my nap made it dark outside.' This faulty particular-to-particular reasoning, bypassing general or logical principles, is called:
explanation: Transductive reasoning links two particular events causally without a general principle connecting them — a hallmark limitation of pre-operational thought, distinct from proper deductive or inductive logic.
